hero.headline: St. Lucie County Fire District terminates 3 firefighters, releases hazing investigation reports
hero.body:
St. Lucie County Fire District on Saturday released investigative reports detailing allegations of hazing and workplace misconduct that led to the termination of 3 firefighters and the suspension of 2 others. According to the district, administrators first received videos in March 2026 showing what they described as senior firefighters using a modified bug zapper to administer electric shocks to probationary and apprentice firefighters while on duty. The district said the incidents occurred during shifts in March and September 2024. The videos prompted Fire Chief Jeff Lee to hire an outside attorney to conduct an independent investigation rather than handle the matter internally.

Attorney J.K. Keller of Allen, Norton & Blue concluded that a preponderance of the evidence showed probationary employees had been subjected to hazing by senior firefighters and supervisors. The investigative report describes videos showing probationary firefighters being questioned while connected to the modified device and receiving electrical shocks when they answered incorrectly. Other videos allegedly show probationary firefighters voluntarily allowing themselves to be shocked while coworkers looked on. Investigators concluded that any claimed consent was undermined by the power imbalance between senior firefighters and probationary employees. Keller also determined the conduct violated multiple district policies, including workplace violence and employee conduct rules.

The district said it followed Keller's recommendations by terminating 3 employees and issuing 48-hour unpaid suspensions to 2 others. The media advisory also includes a separate 2025 workplace culture assessment by attorney Susan Gainey, who found Station 1A had an environment marked by intense peer pressure, social exclusion and light hazing that blurred the line between camaraderie and misconduct. Although that earlier investigation did not substantiate harassment claims, Gainey recommended reassigning personnel and implementing additional leadership and workplace culture training.

The disciplined employees have exercised their contractual rights to challenge the actions through the grievance and arbitration process. The district said it will confidently present these documented facts within that legal forum and will have no further public comment at this time. Fire Chief Lee chose to bring in independent legal counsel to examine the allegations after receiving the videos rather than conducting an internal review of the incidents that occurred nearly two years before they came to light.

cards.headline: Waterspouts, lightning strikes and fires hit Port St. Lucie and Sebastian during severe weather
cards.teaser: Severe weather on Friday brought waterspouts, lightning strikes and fires across the Treasure Coast, with Port St. Lucie fire crews responding to a brush fire and house fire and a man airlifted to the hospital in Okeechobee County after a lightning strike.
cards.body:
Friday's severe weather left a trail of impacts across the Treasure Coast and Palm Beach County. Video sent to the WPTV newsroom from Sebastian showed a large waterspout passing over the Indian River Lagoon Friday afternoon. In Port St. Lucie, WPTV weather spotters captured video of heavy rain moving through the area. Merry Moore O'Rourke said her rain gauge caught over 3 inches. "All of a sudden, it got black. The wind started just raging and the sky had lit up like I have not seen," Moore O'Rourke said.

Severe weather stretched all the way to Okeechobee County, where fire rescue crews airlifted a man to the hospital after he was struck by lightning. Port St. Lucie also saw significant lightning activity. Lucie County Fire District said crews contained a brush fire near the 1900 block of Castinet Lane after reports that a lightning strike ignited vegetation in a nearby lot. At the 900 block of Bellevue Avenue, fire crews responded to an evening house fire. WPTV radar picked up a significant amount of lightning in the area at the time of the storm. Lucie County Fire District said it cannot confirm the cause, as the fire marshal's office still needs to investigate. Moore O'Rourke summed up what many across the region felt as the storms moved through. "I mean it was radical. I mean it was a little scary," Moore O'Rourke said.

cards.headline: JetBlue cancels Vero Beach to JFK route in September, cites low demand
cards.body:
JetBlue is canceling its flight route between Vero Beach Regional Airport and New York's JFK Airport, with the last flights operating on Sept. 9. The airline cited low demand as the reason for ending the route, which launched last December to excitement from Treasure Coast residents hoping for convenient travel options to the Northeast. Brandon Dambeck, interim airport director, said the decision reflects how the airline industry operates. "It's just the way that that market works, and air carriers will fluctuate based off of demand," Dambeck said. He explained that JetBlue was not seeing the ridership numbers it had hoped for on the JFK route. "Just wasn't seeing what they were hoping for," Dambeck said. All affected customers will be notified directly by JetBlue and will receive full refunds.

Not everyone agrees the route had a fair shot. Charlie Ahern, who regularly uses JetBlue flights at Vero Beach Regional Airport, said he believes the route would have grown over time. "I think if they hung in there, it would have worked. I think it would have built up pretty good," Ahern said. He emphasized the convenience of flying out of Vero Beach. "It's easy. It's close," Ahern said. Meanwhile, Grece Ezzi flew into Vero Beach on JetBlue from Boston on Friday for the first time. Dambeck said that route is performing well and seeing strong ridership. "Boston is seeing great demand," Dambeck said.

As for whether the JFK route could return in the future, Dambeck said the door is not closed. "They'll evaluate continuously. So just because it's gone now doesn't mean that it never will come back," Dambeck said. JetBlue has not announced whether it plans to add any replacement routes from Vero Beach or if it will adjust frequency on the remaining Boston service. The airline's decision comes less than a year after the route was introduced, suggesting the service struggled to attract sufficient passengers during its initial months of operation.

Passengers with upcoming reservations on the discontinued route are encouraged to contact JetBlue directly or check their email for rebooking options and refund information. The cancellation leaves Vero Beach Regional Airport with continued service to Boston, which Dambeck indicated is performing significantly better than the New York route. The contrast between the two routes highlights the challenges airlines face when launching new service to smaller regional airports, where passenger demand can be difficult to predict and sustain.

cards.headline: Cardinals Homer Twice, Defeat St. Lucie Mets 7-4
cards.teaser:
The St. Lucie Mets fell behind early and could not complete a late comeback in a 7-4 loss to the Palm Beach Cardinals on Saturday at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium.

The loss evened
cards.body:
The St. Lucie Mets fell behind early and could not complete a late comeback in a 7-4 loss to the Palm Beach Cardinals on Saturday at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium.

The loss evened the three-game series at one game apiece and set up a rubber match Sunday afternoon.

Palm Beach opened the scoring with three runs in the bottom of the first inning. Brayden Smith singled to center field, and an error by D'Andre Smith allowed the Cardinals to capitalize. Ryan Weingartner and Sebastian Dos Santos scored on the play before Brayden Smith came around to give Palm Beach a 3-0 advantage.

St. Lucie responded with two runs in the second inning.

Chase Meggers delivered an RBI single with runners on the corners, scoring AJ Salgado. Jeremy Rodriguez then brought Simon Juan home on a fielder's choice to cut the Cardinals' lead to 3-2.

Palm Beach began pulling away in the fourth inning. Alex Birg drove in Yordalin Pena with an RBI single before Dos Santos launched a two-run home run. The Cardinals eventually built a 7-2 lead.

The Mets bullpen settled the game down after Joe Scarborough entered from the bullpen. Scarborough delivered two scoreless and hitless innings while striking out four batters.

It marked Scarborough's second consecutive scoreless appearance at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium.

Antonio Jimenez gave the Mets another run in the top of the sixth inning with a solo home run. It was Jimenez's sixth homer of the season and his fourth during July, cutting the Palm Beach lead to 7-3.

Caden Wooster followed Scarborough with another strong relief appearance. Wooster allowed just one hit over two scoreless innings and struck out four.

Scarborough and Wooster combined to strike out eight batters over four shutout innings. St. Lucie's pitching staff finished the game with 12 strikeouts, reaching double digits for the second consecutive night.

The Mets mounted one final rally in the ninth inning and brought the potential tying run to the plate. Palm Beach reliever Nathan Shinn escaped the threat and secured the victory for the Cardinals.

St. Lucie fell to 7-14 in the second half and 40-47 overall. Palm Beach improved to 13-9 in the second half and 65-42 overall.

The teams will decide the series Sunday at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium. First pitch is scheduled for 12:30 p.m.

cards.headline: Florida Rep. Fabian Basabe Ordered to Pay $450,000 in Sexual Harassment Case
cards.teaser: A Leon County jury found Republican state Rep. Fabian Basabe liable for sexual harassment, battery and defamation, ordering him to pay $450,000.
cards.body:
Republican state Rep. Fabian Basabe ended the week facing a $450,000 civil judgment after a Leon County jury found him liable for sexual harassment, battery and defamation. The case was brought by former legislative aide Nicolas Frevola, former intern Jacob Cutbirth and Frevola's mother. Basabe represented himself despite having no legal training. The trial was repeatedly interrupted by procedural mistakes and violations of the judge's orders. Circuit Judge J. Lee Marsh told him that if an attorney had done half of what he had done, they would have been sanctioned.

Basabe told jurors he represented himself because he wanted to demonstrate that he had nothing to hide. After the verdict, however, he acknowledged that proceeding without an attorney was a mistake. Basabe continues to deny the underlying allegations. He has not been criminally charged, and an outside ethics investigation conducted for the Florida House previously reached an inconclusive finding. His political opponents quickly called for his resignation. Basabe is seeking reelection this fall, and the verdict could also renew questions about whether House leaders will pursue disciplinary action.

cards.headline: Florida Lawmaker Angie Nixon Gets September Trial Date on Capitol Sit-In Charges
cards.teaser: Democratic state Rep. Angie Nixon will stand trial the week of September 21 on misdemeanor charges stemming from her May sit-in outside Gov. Ron DeSantis' Capitol office.
cards.body:
Nixon and other protesters occupied the area outside DeSantis's office for several hours while objecting to Florida's newly approved congressional map, which could help Republicans add up to four seats in the U.S. House. Capitol Police arrested Nixon after she refused an order to leave. Nixon calls the prosecution political and has incorporated the case into her campaign for U.S. Senate.

The trial is scheduled after Florida's August 18 primary, in which Nixon is challenging retired Army Lt. Alex Vindman for the Democratic Senate nomination. Nixon said following Wednesday's hearing that the threat of a trial will not make her back down.

Vindman raised $8.5 million during the second quarter and has pushed his total receipts above $16 million. Republican Sen. Ashley Moody reported raising another $3.6 million. Moody was appointed to the Senate after Marco Rubio resigned to become secretary of state. The November special election will determine who serves the final two years of Rubio's term.

cards.headline: Trump's National Address Puts Spotlight on Florida Voter Registration Data
cards.teaser: President Donald Trump's Thursday address renewed debate over election security as newly released intelligence records referenced publicly available Florida voter registration data.
cards.body:
President Donald Trump's national address Thursday renewed debate over election security as he urged Congress to adopt tighter voting restrictions. "Mail-in ballots are inherently corrupt," Trump said during the address, repeating claims about the 2020 election that have not been substantiated. Trump did not single out Florida, but declassified records released by his White House did. One declassified report says a Chinese cyber actor downloaded publicly available Florida voter-registration information from commercial websites in 2022. The same actor also obtained records from Colorado, Connecticut, Michigan, Oklahoma and Rhode Island. Another intelligence record lists Florida among 18 states whose voter information was obtained for possible identity matching and public-opinion analysis.

The records describe the collection of voter information, some of it publicly available, but do not say Florida ballots or vote totals were altered. The 2022 report also says the actor's motive was unknown. The White House characterized the broader collection effort as a major compromise of American voter data. However, an earlier federal assessment of the 2022 elections found no evidence that detected foreign cyber activity prevented voting, changed votes or compromised the integrity of ballots.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County Sheriff ramps up traffic enforcement after 1,162 stops in four weeks
cards.teaser: St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office is intensifying traffic enforcement this summer, deploying additional deputies to target speeding and reckless driving on Midway Road, U.S. Highway 1 and Indian River Drive.
cards.body:
St. Lucie County Sheriff Richard Del Toro said traffic is the top concern among residents and described the crackdown as a quality of life issue. Del Toro is using extra deputies from the sheriff's school resource division to boost enforcement while the school year is on break. He is also placing top-performing deputies in areas of concern. Deputies Christopher Rodrigues and Cheyenne Benning are among those targeting high-problem corridors, including Midway Road, U.S. Highway 1 and Indian River Drive. Benning said the county sees a lot of excessive speeding, noting that someone recently passed her on I-95 doing 105 mph. Rodrigues described stops on those same roads, including a driver doing 72 mph on Midway Road, another doing 98 mph on U.S. Highway 1, and a top speed of 73 mph on Indian River Drive, where the limit is 25 mph.

In the past four weeks, deputies conducted 1,162 traffic stops, wrote 470 citations and issued 1,728 written warnings. The enforcement push is part of a broader strategy Del Toro put in place when he took office. He eliminated the agency's dedicated traffic unit and made traffic enforcement the responsibility of every deputy. Since 2025, the sheriff's office has issued more than 26,000 citations, a 155% increase.

cards.headline: Florida fentanyl summit in Orlando draws teens, grieving parents and DEA chief
cards.teaser: Teens from anti-drug coalitions across the country joined grieving parents and DEA Administrator Terrance Cole at the Fentanyl Free America Summit in Orlando this week to discuss stopping fentanyl deaths.
cards.body:
The Fentanyl Free America Summit in Orlando drew students from anti-drug coalitions across the country who traveled to Florida to learn about the resurgence of fentanyl. Hannah Kahn, 18, explained what brought her to the summit, saying she has a relative addicted to methamphetamine and seeing how that destroyed his life encouraged her to prevent that from happening to others. Jasmine Figueroa, 19, offered pointed advice for adults on how to talk to young people about drugs, saying it is not a taboo topic and adults should tell them what cocaine is because they're going to get educated one way or another.

This year's summit welcomed the U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration as a partner. DEA Administrator Terrance Cole spent time with victim families and discussed the ongoing threat, saying the poison is being manufactured and distributed out of Mexico by the Mexican cartels. Cole pointed to new tools from the current administration, explaining the president has designated the cartels as foreign terrorists, which opens different avenues for the DEA to target. Mari Rodriguez's daughter, Imam, died of fentanyl poisoning in 2023 after making the mistake of buying a Percocet pill that had fentanyl in it. Rodriguez said the fight against fentanyl should have started in 2009, when the first fentanyl was found on American streets.

hero.headline: Britain's Josh Kerr breaks mile world record that stood for 27 years
hero.teaser: Josh Kerr ran the mile in 3:42.66 Saturday in London, breaking Hicham El Guerrouj's previous mark of 3:43.13 set in 1999. Kerr's sponsor dubbed the effort Project 222, referencing the number of seconds in 3 minutes, 42 seconds.
hero.body:
Great Britain's Josh Kerr ran the mile in 3:42.66 Saturday in London, breaking Hicham El Guerrouj's world record of 3:43.13 set in 1999. Kerr made no secret that he was targeting the long-standing record at Saturday's Diamond League event. Earlier this week, he revealed he ran 2:42.45 in a 1,200-meter time trial. His sponsor, Brooks, dubbed the effort "Project 222," referencing the number of seconds in 3 minutes, 42 seconds. The shoe company said Friday that this is the moment Josh Kerr stands to make history and bring the mile record home. American Yared Nuguse finished second in 3:45.69.

Kerr has emerged as one of the world's top middle-distance runners, winning bronze in the 1,500 meters at the Tokyo Olympics and silver at the 2024 Paris Olympics. Before turning professional, Kerr starred at the University of New Mexico, where he won multiple NCAA titles and set an NCAA indoor mile record of 3:35.01 in 2018. Kerr's record-setting run came during the Diamond League, an established international circuit of professional track and field events.

cards.headline: Argentina defeats England 2-1 with late goals to reach World Cup final
cards.teaser: Argentina rallied from a 1-0 deficit with two late goals to defeat England 2-1 in the World Cup semifinals. The defending champions will face Spain in the final Sunday in East Rutherford, New Jersey.
cards.body:
Argentina scored two goals in the final minutes to defeat England 2-1 in the World Cup semifinals Wednesday. Trailing 1-0 going into the 85th minute after England's Anthony Gordon scored in the 55th minute, Argentina rallied with goals from Enzo Fernandez and substitute Lautaro Martinez. Fernandez scored the equalizer in the 85th minute after receiving the ball from Lionel Messi and sweeping it in from outside the box. Martinez headed in the winner two minutes into stoppage time from a Messi cross.

The loss marks the third time England has fallen in the World Cup semifinals after losses to Germany in 1990 and Croatia in 2018. England captain Harry Kane said the team worked hard to reach the semifinals and falling short was gutting. England coach Thomas Tuchel said Argentina played with more risk and rhythm while England played with the feeling they had a lot to lose.

Argentina will face Spain in the final Sunday in East Rutherford, New Jersey. The defending champions have repeatedly fought back at this year's World Cup from difficult positions. Argentina coach Lionel Scaloni said the team showed collectiveness and brotherhood in fighting to the very end. Messi, now 39 and likely playing at his last World Cup, is one win away from further strengthening his case as the greatest soccer player of all time.

cards.headline: MLB restricts dugout iPad use to prevent artificial intelligence from making game decisions
cards.teaser: Major League Baseball made custom tabs on dugout iPads inaccessible to teams starting Wednesday to prevent use of artificial intelligence to help make in-game decisions. The tablets had been used for recommendations on substitutions and pitch calling.
cards.body:
Major League Baseball made custom tabs on dugout iPads inaccessible to teams starting Wednesday night when the second half of the season started. The league is restricting iPad usage in dugouts to prevent the tablets from running artificial intelligence to help make decisions. The tablets have access to video and league-provided data, and also included a custom tab where teams could access other programs.

MLB executive vice president of baseball operations Morgan Sword wrote in a June 11 memo to general managers, assistant GMs and video coordinators that in many cases, the custom tab had expanded the use of the dugout iPads beyond their originally intended purpose to include recommendations regarding substitutions, pitch calling, and other in-game decisions traditionally made by players and coaches. A review by the competition committee found clubs had been compliant with the regulations. Sword wrote that instituting this prohibition beginning with the second half of the season is intended to provide clubs that have relied on the custom tab with appropriate lead-time to make any necessary adjustments. MLB started a pilot program allowing use of iPads in dugouts with restrictions late in the 2015 season and expanded their use in 2016 under a deal with Apple. Video was eliminated in the 2020 COVID season following the Houston Astros' sign-stealing scandal, then returned in 2021.

cards.headline: Photographer's 2007 images of Messi bathing Yamal as baby resurface before World Cup final
cards.teaser: Photographer Joan Monfort took photos in 2007 of teenage Lionel Messi bathing infant Lamine Yamal in a plastic bathtub for a charity calendar. The 19-year-old Yamal will face 39-year-old Messi in Sunday's World Cup final.
cards.body:
Photographer Joan Monfort took photos in 2007 of a teenage Lionel Messi bathing a baby boy in a plastic bathtub as part of a charity calendar produced by local newspaper Sport and UNICEF. The baby was Lamine Yamal, who is now 19 years old and will face Messi in Sunday's World Cup final when Argentina plays Spain. Monfort, who works as a freelance photojournalist for the AP, said luck dictated that Yamal's mother won a raffle of families in the city of Mataró, near Barcelona, who wanted to participate. A tearful Messi left Barcelona in 2021 when the club was in financial trouble, and Yamal erupted at the club two years later.

Monfort had no recollection of the photos until Yamal's father posted one on social media during the 2024 European Championship, when a teenage Yamal was enjoying his international breakout and led Spain to the title. The photo went viral then, but with the World Cup final looming, Monfort said interest in his photos has skyrocketed. He said the fact that the final is in the U.S. has given it extra push. Monfort, 58, is a lifelong Barcelona supporter and said his heart is split between the two teams. He said he has an everlasting love for Messi, the best player of all time, but Yamal has broken the mold and represents a new, diverse Spain, thanks to his parents from Morocco and Equatorial Guinea. Monfort is considering traveling to see the final in New Jersey.

cards.headline: Security ramped up for World Cup final with Secret Service perimeter for Trump attendance
cards.teaser: The World Cup final Sunday in New Jersey will include enhanced Secret Service security with President Trump attending the trophy presentation. A joint operations center has overseen security throughout the tournament.
cards.body:
The 2026 FIFA World Cup final Sunday in New Jersey will include a beefed-up Secret Service perimeter, with President Trump attending the trophy presentation. White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt says his attendance will cap what has been the most watched, most secure, and most successful World Cup in American history. The final is a Level 1 Special Event, the highest possible security designation, with added resources from the Department of Homeland Security, the Department of Defense, and the FBI.

A joint operations center in New York has helped oversee security and monitor threats in host cities throughout the tournament. The FBI has seized hundreds of drones flying in restricted airspace near stadiums during the tournament. FBI Special Agent Adam Kachhia-Patel says the agency will be getting live feeds and monitoring any drone activity in the area to see if there is anything that needs to be done from a threat perspective. No one will be allowed to simply walk up to the stadium or drive a personal vehicle. Those with a ticket must take approved transportation to the game and should arrive early to make their way through the stepped-up security. When Trump attended an NBA Finals game last month in New York, police shut down several city blocks around the arena and fans were forced to wait in extra-long lines to go through enhanced security.

cards.headline: Flip City Gym and Cheer gymnasts earn top 15 national finish, qualify for Junior Olympics
cards.body:
Three gymnasts from Flip City Gym and Cheer secured a top 15 finish at AAU Nationals in Knoxville, Tennessee last month and qualified for the Junior Olympics in Iowa next month. Skylar Rose-Daris, Victoria Supan, and Charli Rine each found their way to gymnastics through different paths. Rose-Daris said it wasn't really gymnastics, it was the fact that she knew how to do a cartwheel. Supan said all the gymnasts that she saw on YouTube, and how amazing they are, and how fun it looks. Rine said she loves it because she learns new things.

Head Coach Candice Lazuka said the team had a really good season. The gymnasts competed locally, traveled, and went to states and regionals. At AAU Nationals in Knoxville, the team came close to a perfect score. Lazuka said it's hard to get a perfect 10, but they got a 9.9 and were very close to a 10. Rose-Daris said it's going to be really fun that she's going to an entire different part of the world. Supan said it's happy and exciting at the same time. When asked what she is focused on heading into the Junior Olympics, Rine said getting first place on floors.

Basabe told jurors he represented himself because he wanted to demonstrate that he had nothing to hide. After the verdict, however, he acknowledged that proceeding without an attorney was a mistake. Basabe continues to deny the underlying allegations. He has not been criminally charged, and an outside ethics investigation conducted for the Florida House previously reached an inconclusive finding. His political opponents quickly called for his resignation. Basabe is seeking reelection this fall, and the verdict could also renew questions about whether House leaders will pursue disciplinary action.

cards.headline: Florida Lawmaker Angie Nixon Gets September Trial Date on Capitol Sit-In Charges
cards.teaser: Democratic state Rep. Angie Nixon will stand trial the week of September 21 on misdemeanor charges stemming from her May sit-in outside Gov. Ron DeSantis' Capitol office.
cards.body:
Nixon and other protesters occupied the area outside DeSantis's office for several hours while objecting to Florida's newly approved congressional map, which could help Republicans add up to four seats in the U.S. House. Capitol Police arrested Nixon after she refused an order to leave. Nixon calls the prosecution political and has incorporated the case into her campaign for U.S. Senate.

The trial is scheduled after Florida's August 18 primary, in which Nixon is challenging retired Army Lt. Alex Vindman for the Democratic Senate nomination. Nixon said following Wednesday's hearing that the threat of a trial will not make her back down.

Vindman raised $8.5 million during the second quarter and has pushed his total receipts above $16 million. Republican Sen. Ashley Moody reported raising another $3.6 million. Moody was appointed to the Senate after Marco Rubio resigned to become secretary of state. The November special election will determine who serves the final two years of Rubio's term.

cards.headline: Trump's National Address Puts Spotlight on Florida Voter Registration Data
cards.teaser: President Donald Trump's Thursday address renewed debate over election security as newly released intelligence records referenced publicly available Florida voter registration data.
cards.body:
President Donald Trump's national address Thursday renewed debate over election security as he urged Congress to adopt tighter voting restrictions. "Mail-in ballots are inherently corrupt," Trump said during the address, repeating claims about the 2020 election that have not been substantiated. Trump did not single out Florida, but declassified records released by his White House did. One declassified report says a Chinese cyber actor downloaded publicly available Florida voter-registration information from commercial websites in 2022. The same actor also obtained records from Colorado, Connecticut, Michigan, Oklahoma and Rhode Island. Another intelligence record lists Florida among 18 states whose voter information was obtained for possible identity matching and public-opinion analysis.

The records describe the collection of voter information, some of it publicly available, but do not say Florida ballots or vote totals were altered. The 2022 report also says the actor's motive was unknown. The White House characterized the broader collection effort as a major compromise of American voter data. However, an earlier federal assessment of the 2022 elections found no evidence that detected foreign cyber activity prevented voting, changed votes or compromised the integrity of ballots.

cards.headline: DEA Administrator Joins Florida Fentanyl Summit as Crisis Takes Center Stage
cards.teaser: The Fentanyl Free America Summit in Orlando drew teens from anti-drug coalitions across the country, grieving parents and DEA Administrator Terrance Cole.
cards.body:
Teens from anti-drug coalitions across the country attended the Fentanyl Free America Summit in Orlando this week alongside grieving parents and federal law enforcement. Hannah Kahn, 18, explained that fentanyl is not widely recognized as a threat because people are not seeking it out directly but rather it is laced within other drugs. Jasmine Figueroa, 19, had pointed advice for adults on discussing drugs with young people, saying it should not be a taboo topic and that teens will get educated one way or another, so adults might as well educate them first and tell them the truth.

This year's summit welcomed the U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration as a partner. DEA Administrator Terrance Cole spent time with victim families and explained that the poison is being manufactured and distributed out of Mexico by the Mexican cartels. Cole pointed to new tools from the current administration, stating that President Trump designated Mexican cartels as foreign terrorists, which opens different avenues for targeting. Mari Rodriguez's daughter, Imam, died of fentanyl poisoning in 2023 after buying a Percocet pill that had fentanyl in it. Rodriguez said the fight should have started in 2009, when the first fentanyl was found on streets. While deaths from the synthetic opioid are down, tracking how widespread fentanyl has become is nearly impossible in part because of Narcan, an over-the-counter nasal spray that is increasing survival rates.

cards.headline: Security First Insurance Lowers Homeowners Rates by Average 5.6% in Florida
cards.teaser: Security First Insurance is lowering homeowners insurance rates by an average of 5.6%, the latest in a series of rate decreases the Florida-based company has made over the last two years.
cards.body:
Security First Insurance is lowering homeowners insurance rates by an average of 5.6%, the latest in a series of rate decreases the Florida-based company has made over the last two years. Melissa Burt DeVriese, president of Security First, said customers are seeing the impact of the rate decreases. Insurance companies have been reducing rates or holding them stable as more companies cite a reduction in lawsuits from state reforms. Burt DeVriese said all those savings the company is required to pass along to customers have been passed along.

Security First also announced new discounts and a disappearing deductible that rewards claims-free customers by reducing their deductible over time. Over the course of five years, every year the deductible goes down 20 percent as long as the customer does not have a loss. Once a loss occurs, the discounted deductible applies and then resets back to the full deductible amount. Based in Ormond Beach, Security First has about 155,000 policies in the state and is committed to writing more policies in southeast Florida. Premiums in South Florida generally run high. Online firm Insurify reports that in 2026 Florida homeowners pay the highest average premium in the country at $8,292. State insurance regulators said that with more companies and more competition, homeowners should seek better premiums by shopping around.

cards.headline: Florida Republican Gubernatorial Candidate Faces Antisemitism Ad and Residency Challenge
cards.teaser: Florida gubernatorial candidate James Fishback faces a $400,000 attack ad and a court hearing over whether he meets the state's seven-year residency requirement for governors.
cards.body:
Businessman James Fishback is facing pressure on two fronts in Florida's Republican gubernatorial primary. The Front Line, a Republican group aligned with U.S. Sen. Ted Cruz, announced a $400,000 campaign targeting Fishback over statements the group characterizes as antisemitic. The artificial intelligence-generated ad depicts Fishback as a talking fish making racist comments. Fishback denies being antisemitic and says the spending shows Republican establishment figures are concerned about his campaign.

Lt. Gov. Jay Collins is challenging Fishback's candidacy, alleging Fishback lived and voted in Washington, D.C., and does not meet Florida's seven-year residency requirement for governors. A two-day hearing is scheduled to begin July 21 in Tallahassee. Fishback says he was born and raised in Florida, has lived in the state throughout his life and purchased a Washington condo only to visit his parents. Because ballots have already been printed, the judge said a ruling against Fishback would likely involve directing election officials not to count votes cast for him rather than removing his name from ballots. A Tyson Group survey released this week placed Fishback at 8% in the Republican primary.

cards.headline: Byron Donalds, David Jolly Lead Florida Governor's Race as Primary Nears
cards.body:
Republican U.S. Rep. Byron Donalds and Democrat David Jolly hold commanding positions in Florida's governor's race with the August 18 primary approaching. A Tyson Group survey released this week placed Donalds at 48% among Republicans, followed by Lt. Gov. Jay Collins at 9%, businessman James Fishback at 8%, and former Florida House Speaker Paul Renner at 4%. About 26% of respondents remained undecided. Donalds has raised more than $90 million across his campaign operation and received President Donald Trump's endorsement. Collins, appointed lieutenant governor by Gov. Ron DeSantis in August 2025, has not received DeSantis's endorsement. Collins used a Thursday campaign call to position himself as the strongest alternative to Donalds and urged Renner to leave the race, saying the primary is between Donalds and himself.

Fishback faces pressure on two fronts. The Front Line, a Republican group aligned with U.S. Sen. Ted Cruz, announced a $400,000 campaign targeting Fishback over statements the group characterizes as antisemitic. The artificial intelligence-generated ad depicts Fishback as a talking fish making racist comments. Collins is also challenging whether Fishback meets Florida's seven-year residency requirement for governors, with a two-day hearing scheduled to begin July 21 in Tallahassee. On the Democratic side, Jolly moved this week to address his past business and political relationship with Clearwater financier Leo Govoni. Federal prosecutors allege Govoni and accountant John Witeck stole more than $100 million from a nonprofit managing trust funds for people with disabilities, with the alleged scheme operating from 2009 through 2025. Jolly previously worked as a vice president at Boston Finance Group, a Govoni-controlled company, and Govoni served as a finance co-chairman during Jolly's unsuccessful 2016 U.S. Senate campaign. Jolly is not a defendant in the case.

hero.headline: Palm Beach County man leads Martin County deputies on 100 mph chase through Indiantown
hero.teaser: Markell Tillman, 33, drove more than 100 mph on State Road 710 before leading deputies on a high-speed chase through Indiantown and onto SW Martin Highway toward Palm City.
hero.body:
A Palm Beach County man led Martin County deputies on a high-speed chase through Indiantown after driving more than 100 mph on State Road 710, one of the area's most dangerous roads. Deputies spotted 33-year-old Markell Tillman driving aggressively at speeds exceeding 100 mph, forcing other vehicles off the roadway. When deputies attempted to stop him, Tillman fled. Tillman weaved through traffic in an attempt to lose deputies before turning onto SW Martin Highway toward Palm City, where he continued to drive recklessly.

Deputies spotted Tillman again traveling eastbound on Martin Highway near Allapattah Road. Deputies used stop sticks to disable his vehicle near I-95. Tillman then bailed out of the vehicle and attempted to flee on foot before deputies caught up with him and took him into custody. Tillman was arrested on charges including fleeing and eluding, aggravated fleeing with injury or damage, operating a vehicle exceeding the speed limit by 50 or more mph, driving while license suspended or revoked, obstruction without violence, and operating a vehicle at 100 or more mph. Tillman also had an out-of-county warrant at the time of his arrest. He was booked into the Martin County Jail.

cards.headline: Martin County faces $2.1 billion transportation funding gap over next 20 years
cards.teaser: Martin County will need approximately $2.8 billion for transportation improvements over the next 20 years but only $701 million is currently available, leaving nine needed road widening projects unfunded.
cards.body:
Martin County is facing a $2.1 billion transportation funding shortfall that could shape how residents get around for decades. The Martin County Metropolitan Planning Organization estimates the county will need approximately $2.8 billion for transportation improvements over the next 20 years, but only $701 million is currently available. This means the county can fund just about one quarter of its identified needs. Of the $701 million currently available, all but $10 million comes from state and federal funding sources.

Nine roads identified as requiring widening as traffic grows remain completely unfunded, with a total cost of approximately $213 million. These roads include SW Martin Downs Boulevard, SR-714/SW Martin Highway, SW 96th Street, SW Bridge Road, CR-714/SW Martin Highway, SW Allapattah Road/CR-609, SE Green River Parkway, SW Indiantown Avenue, and SE Bridge Road/CR-708. May and Maddy Brumlow, who travel Martin Downs Boulevard nearly every day, said the congestion is already noticeable.

Beth Beltran, administrator for Martin County's Metropolitan Planning Organization, said funding shortfalls of this scale are not unusual and that she does not know of one MPO in the whole country where the needs are equal to the revenue. State Road 710 is among the county's highest priorities due to safety concerns. The draft Cost Feasible Plan includes several SR-710 projects that are already funded or programmed, including a realignment at CR-714/Martin Highway and widening from CR-609 to SW Van Buren Road, totaling nearly $300 million.

cards.headline: Jonathan Dickinson State Park concession closed indefinitely, boat rentals and tours suspended
cards.teaser: The concession operation at Jonathan Dickinson State Park is closed indefinitely after the vendor's contract expired, leaving visitors without access to boat rentals, canoe rentals, and the Loxahatchee Queen tour to Trapper Nelson's Island.
cards.body:
Jonathan Dickinson State Park's concession operation is closed indefinitely this summer, leaving visitors without access to boat rentals, canoe rentals, and the popular Loxahatchee Queen tour to Trapper Nelson's Island. Park officials told WPTV the vendor who operated the concession had their contract expire. The park is now searching for a new vendor, but warns the approval process is lengthy and could take months.

Max Santos, a Jupiter local who has been coming to the park his entire life, said he and others were caught off guard when they arrived to find the concession office closed. Santos said the concession had allowed visitors to access bike rentals, canoes, motorboats, and tours, and provided a place to get refreshments after activities. Daniela Sellitti drove from West Palm Beach with her kids hoping to take them on the Loxahatchee Queen to Trapper Nelson's Island, only to find the service unavailable. The park website lists the concession as closed indefinitely. Sellitti said she hopes the park finds a contract with someone else to reopen the concession and get the boats running again so visitors can enjoy the river and visit Trapper Nelson's.

cards.headline: Safe Kids Treasure Coast offering free pool alarms to Martin County residents
cards.teaser: The Florida Department of Health and Safe Kids Treasure Coast are providing a limited supply of free pool alarms to qualifying Martin County residents with residential pools.
cards.body: The Florida Department of Health and Safe Kids Treasure Coast are providing a limited supply of free pool alarms to qualifying residents in Martin County. A pool alarm is one layer of protection and should always be used alongside close adult supervision, pool barriers and water safety education to help prevent drowning, the coalition said. The program is available to Martin County residents with a residential pool, with one alarm per household and no income or priority group requirements. Alarms are available while supplies last. A 9-volt battery is required to operate the alarm but is not included. Safe Kids Treasure Coast is asking residents to fill out an online survey to determine eligibility. For more information, residents can call (772) 462-3501.

cards.headline: Two Martin County brush fires contained, more expected this summer
cards.teaser: Martin County saw two brush fires this week, including one sparked by a lightning strike, both now fully contained and being monitored by the Florida Forest Service.
cards.body:
Martin County saw two brush fires this week, including one sparked by a lightning strike. Both are now fully contained and being monitored by the Florida Forest Service. The Florida Forest Service says the conditions that fuel these fires are not going away anytime soon, but residents should not be alarmed.

David Grubitch, a mitigation specialist and spokesperson with the department, said this is their peak season. The summertime heat is drying out fine dead fuels, making them receptive when lightning strikes occur. Grubitch explained that rain often extinguishes these fires immediately, but sometimes they travel underground and surface days later. He said the public plays a crucial role in helping the Florida Forest Service do its job. Grubitch stressed that residents should never assume someone else has already called in a brush fire. If you see something, say something, as he said, it can make all the difference in how quickly crews are able to get a fire under control.

cards.headline: Hobe Sound couple seeks support as husband battles head and neck cancer
cards.teaser: Dave and Faren Motz of Hobe Sound are asking for community support as Dave battles head and neck cancer, facing nearly $20,000 in out-of-pocket costs for treatment.
cards.body:
A Hobe Sound couple is asking for community support as they navigate a cancer diagnosis. Dave and Faren Motz met in South Florida before moving to Maui, where they married and raised their family. Faren homeschooled all three of their children, and the family started a farm where they served children. Years later, the couple moved to Hobe Sound and purchased a property, but just months after settling in, Dave was diagnosed with head and neck cancer.

As the couple searched for healthcare in Florida, AdventHealth in Celebration provided programs and grants that became a critical resource. Dave underwent nearly seven weeks of daily radiation treatments. The repeated visits to Orlando, biopsies, scans, and exams added up, costing the couple nearly $20,000 out of pocket. Their age and income kept them from qualifying for Medicare or Medicaid. Dave, a former firefighter who had long been the family's provider, now has an 85% chance of recovery according to doctors. Faren now works to support them both at Latitudes at the Jupiter Beach Resort, where those who want to show support can visit. Those who would like to contribute financially can donate to the family's GoFundMe at Standing with Dave Motz in his cancer battle.

cards.headline: Murray Middle School demolition underway after Hurricane Milton tornado damage
cards.body:
Demolition is underway at Murray Middle School in Martin County, marking the start of a major reconstruction effort following tornado damage caused by Hurricane Milton. The project includes reconstruction of buildings destroyed in the tornadoes, along with a new administration building, media center, art lab, and a full overhaul of the parking lot. The demolition phase alone costs $3.3 million, though the total project cost has not been finalized. The project is being funded by local capital improvement, sales tax and Public Education Capital Outlay. Students who were displaced from the affected classrooms will continue learning in portable classrooms until construction is complete.

Kirstie Gernaine, coordinator of public information and community relations for the Martin County School District, said the school was already scheduled for significant construction before the hurricane struck. "Murray Middle School was already slated to get all of this construction work with a new admin area, a new media center and a brand new art lab," said Gernaine. "With Hurricane Milton and those tornadoes destroying the buildings in the back buildings 18, 10, and nine we were able to add these on." The school district said parents can be assured their students will be safe during construction. Barriers have already been placed around the work zone to keep students out. The district hopes to complete the renovations by December 2027.

hero.headline: Sheriff Richard Del Toro ramps up traffic enforcement across St. Lucie County this summer
hero.teaser: St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office is intensifying traffic enforcement this summer, deploying additional deputies to reduce speeding and reckless driving across the county.
hero.body:
Sheriff Richard Del Toro said traffic is the top concern among residents and described the crackdown as a quality of life issue. Del Toro is using extra deputies from the sheriff's school resource division to boost enforcement while the school year is on break. He is also placing top-performing deputies in areas of concern. Deputies Christopher Rodrigues and Cheyenne Benning are among those targeting high-problem corridors, including Midway Road, U.S. Highway 1 and Indian River Drive.

Benning said the office sees a lot of excessive speeding in St. Lucie County. She said most recently she had someone pass her on I-95 doing 105 mph. Rodrigues said he stopped a girl yesterday doing 72 mph on Midway Road and 98 mph on U.S. Highway 1. On Indian River Drive, which has a 25 mph speed limit, his top speed recorded was 73 mph. In the past four weeks, deputies conducted 1,162 traffic stops, wrote 470 citations and issued 1,728 written warnings. The enforcement push is part of a broader strategy Del Toro put in place when he took office. He eliminated the agency's dedicated traffic unit and made traffic enforcement the responsibility of every deputy. Since 2025, the sheriff's office has issued more than 26,000 citations, a 155% increase.

cards.headline: Dale Mincey charged with first-degree murder in fatal shooting of Fort Pierce art teacher Andre Barnes
cards.teaser: St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office announced a second arrest in the fatal shooting of Fort Pierce art teacher Andre Leonard Barnes, 66.
cards.body:
Dale A. Mincey, 41, Barnes' nephew, was formally charged with first-degree murder Saturday in connection with Barnes' death. Mincey remains in custody at the St. Lucie County Jail and is being held without bond. The fatal shooting happened July 7 at a residence on the 2700 block of Essex Drive. Deputies responded to the home at around 3:30 p.m. after receiving reports of a person with a gunshot wound. When deputies arrived, they learned a man had shot another man with a rifle. Barnes was taken to a local hospital, where he died. Deputies said the fatal shooting was premeditated.

Karen Moye, the victim's sister and mother of the suspect, was also at the home when the shooting occurred. She heard a loud bang while she was in the bathroom and came out to find Mincey and called police. Sheriff Richard Del Toro said Tuesday that detectives uncovered information indicating that Moye knowingly provided false information to investigators and withheld pertinent information related to this homicide investigation. She has been charged with false report to law enforcement and the commission of a capital felony. During questioning, Mincey told detectives he could not recall what happened the day of the shooting and that he didn't have any issues with Barnes and did not know how Barnes died. However, he admitted to owning two firearms. Barnes worked as an art teacher for the St. Lucie County School District since 2017, serving at West Gate K-8 and Samuel S. Gaines Academy.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce neighbors pack planning meeting over Causeway Cove high-rise development proposal
cards.teaser: The Causeway Cove development project was reviewed by the Fort Pierce Planning Board on Monday. The project includes five high-rise buildings, including a 17-story building standing 192 feet tall.
cards.body:
The Causeway Cove development project was reviewed by the Fort Pierce Planning Board on Monday. The project, located off Seaway Drive, includes five high-rise buildings, including a 17-story building standing 192 feet tall, more than four times the city's height limit. Plans also call for two hotels and more than 70,000 square feet of retail space. The development qualifies under the Live Local Act, a state law passed in 2023 that allows developers to bypass height and density restrictions as long as they set aside 40% of units for affordable housing for at least 30 years. The project includes more than 900 apartments and condos, with 365 of those designated as affordable housing.

Neighbors packed the chamber during the Monday meeting. Buster Brewster, a boater at Causeway Cove Marina, said he worries the project will change the character of the area. Dennis Fein raised concerns about traffic, saying nobody has thought this out and predicting massive traffic jams with nobody able to get on or off the island. City Planning Director Kev Freeman said developers must add traffic mitigation efforts and any required intersection or access improvements. City Commissioner Michael Broderick said the city has no authority over whether the project is approved, stating the city does not have a play here and this is regulated by the state of Florida in the entirety. City commissioners are scheduled to hear a review of the project as the next step in the process.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie couple fights rezoning of lot behind home near Crosstown Parkway
cards.teaser: A Port St. Lucie couple is searching for answers after the city council voted to rezone the lot behind their home from residential to commercial.
cards.body:
Joseph and Margaret Mucciolo have called Port St. Lucie home since purchasing their property, drawn by what Margaret described as the beautiful setting and backyard views of nature. In a unanimous vote, the Port St. Lucie City Council approved rezoning the lot behind their yard, where trees currently stand, from residential to commercial. One council member said the change is necessary to reduce traffic in the neighborhood, explaining that adding commercial closer to neighborhoods reduces the length of trips, which reduces overall traffic because shorter trips reduce the burden on the overall network.

The Mucciolos fought the rezoning for months and feel their voices have gone unheard. The council held its second reading Monday. While there was public comment, it was what is called a quasi-judicial hearing, meaning council members act as a panel of judges, applying existing zoning rules to a specific property and making decisions based strictly on sworn testimony and factual evidence, not public opinion. The Mucciolos say the process needs to change to be logical, transparent, caring, and provide hope for people. They say they will be exploring any kind of appeal process to change this outcome or to change the next one. Joseph Mucciolo said he believes in six months or a year, the trees behind their home will be gone.

cards.headline: Villa Del Sol residents return home after nearly 2 years following structural damage repairs
cards.teaser: Villa Del Sol residents in St. Lucie County told WPTV they are able to return home after nearly two years of being displaced from their condos.
cards.body:
Residents told WPTV they were notified last month they could return to their condos, after an inspection in August 2024 found structural damage in buildings 3, 4, and 5, which were deemed unsafe. Katie Johnson was the first to share to WPTV that residents had been told they could come back. WPTV received emails sent to residents from the Board of Directors telling them they could return. WPTV also obtained a letter from engineers sent to St. Lucie County's Building Department requesting they lift occupancy restrictions following their special inspection. Katie Johnson described the work still underway at the property, saying they're still moving the dirt back under the buildings.

Robert Segedin took WPTV inside his family's home, excited to return but thinking about those who cannot. Eric Johnson is among those not coming back. He was one of the first residents WPTV met at Villa Del Sol and is now living in Georgia. Eric Johnson said the financial toll has been severe and that he and his family had to drain out all their savings accounts and all their 401ks just trying to make ends meet while this was going on. He is filing for bankruptcy and filing his condo for foreclosure. Katie Johnson said she is thinking of neighbors, like Eric Johnson, who cannot return and feels so bad that some were hit harder than others with the situation.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County woman wins $5 million from scratch-off ticket purchased in Fort Pierce
cards.teaser: Maria Duran, 57, claimed a $5 million top prize from the $5,000,000 CROSSWORD CASH scratch-off game on April 6.
cards.body: Maria Duran, 57, claimed a $5 million top prize from the $5,000,000 CROSSWORD CASH scratch-off game on April 6. Duran chose to receive her winnings as a one-time, lump-sum payment of $3,262,138. Florida Lottery officials said Duran purchased her winning ticket from PK 2 Quick Mart, located at 4101 Okeechobee Road in Fort Pierce. The woman turned $20 into $5 million. The game's overall odds of winning are 1-in-2.90. However, the chance of winning $5 million playing this game is 1-in-4,018,135. Florida Lottery officials announced the jackpot Friday.

hero.headline: Indian River County families can apply for free or reduced-price student meals starting July 15
hero.teaser: Families in Indian River County are able to apply for free or reduced price meals for students starting July 15.
hero.body:
Students at six Indian River County schools can receive free meals during the 2026-2027 school year through federal nutrition programs. Other families in the district may still qualify for free or reduced-price meals based on household size and income criteria. Families are encouraged to complete one application per household to determine eligibility for free or reduced-price school meals.

Families must visit www.LINQConnect.com to sign in or create an account, then search for Indian River County Public Schools in Vero Beach. They need to add their student using the Student ID and the child's formal name as listed in FOCUS. From the website homepage, families click School Services at the top menu, then select Free and Reduced Meal Application.

Families with questions about the meal programs can contact Shawn O'Keefe, the district's nutrition services director, at (772) 564-5041 or shawn.okeefe@indianriverschools.org.
